title: RBI: Notification — Master Direction on Note Sorting Machines
applicability: Machines operated by banks, either directly by their staff or indirectly by their agents
description: RBI has issued a notification concerning Master Direction on Note Sorting Machines.
summary: This Master Direction incorporates and updates extant guidelines, circulars, and directives on Note Sorting Machines, establishing comprehensive minimum standards for note authentication and fitness sorting parameters. It was issued to enable banks to have all current instructions on Note Sorting Machines at one place for reference while withdrawing previous circulars on the subject. In practice, compliance workflows will require banks to evaluate machine sorting against detailed criteria for soiling, limpness, dog-ears, tears, holes, stains, graffiti, crumples/folds, decolouration, and repairs, conduct quarterly testing and calibration, and ensure discontinued models are phased out by June 30, 2027.
takeaway: Ensure that Note Sorting Machines are tested for accuracy and consistency on a quarterly basis, maintain signed certificates for records, phase out discontinued NSM models on or before June 30, 2027, and exclusively procure BIS certified Note Sorting Machines going forward.

title: RBI: Amendment — Local Area Banks Acquisition and Holding of Shares or Voting Rights Amendment Directions 2026
applicability: Mutual funds registered with SEBI, pension funds registered with PFRDA, and insurance companies registered with IRDAI, who are seeking or have obtained one-time approval for subsequent acquisitions of major shareholding up to 10 per cent of the paid-up share capital or voting rights of a local area banking company.
description: RBI has issued a amendment concerning the Reserve Bank of India (Local Area Banks - Acquisition and Holding of Shares or Voting Rights) Amendment Directions, 2026.
summary: The Reserve Bank of India has introduced the Reserve Bank of India (Local Area Banks - Acquisition and Holding of Shares or Voting Rights) Amendment Directions, 2026, which allow qualifying mutual funds, insurance companies, and pension funds to obtain a one-time approval for subsequent acquisitions of major shareholding up to 10 percent of a banking company's paid-up share capital or voting rights. This regulatory change was initiated based on a review to streamline approvals while continuing to ensure oversight of major shareholdings in banking companies. In practice, qualifying persons must now submit applications through PRAVAAH along with Form A, banks must furnish comments in Form A1, and approved entities must report any aggregate holding decreases or increases crossing the five percent threshold to the RBI and the banking company within three working days.
takeaway: Submit applications for one-time approval through PRAVAAH along with Form A, and report any decrease or increase of the aggregate holding to below or above five per cent of the total paid-up share capital or voting rights of the banking company to the Reserve Bank and the concerned banking company within three working days of such an event.

summary: The Board has further extended the last date for submission of all applicable electronic forms PGIRP-1 to PGIRP-6, along with postponing the levy of penalties for delayed submission or modification. This extension is granted in response to feedback and requests received from Insolvency Professionals and Insolvency Professional Agencies seeking additional time to file the forms. In practice, compliance officers now have until the revised deadline to complete filings without incurring penalties for delayed submission.
takeaway: Ensure all applicable PGIRP-1 to PGIRP-6 forms are submitted by 31st December 2026 to avoid penalties for delayed submission or modification.

title: IBBI: Circular — Cessation of Interim Moratorium in respect of personal guarantors to corporate debtors
applicability: All Registered Insolvency Professionals, All Recognised Insolvency Professional Entities, and All Registered Insolvency Professional Agencies
description: IBBI has issued a circular concerning Judgments of the Hon'ble Bombay High Court and Delhi High Court on cessation of interim moratorium in respect of personal guarantors to corporate debtors.
summary: The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (Amendment) Act, 2026 inserted sub-section (4) in sections 96 and 124 of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016, providing that the interim moratorium shall not apply to personal guarantors to corporate debtors starting from May 26, 2026. This circular highlights judgments from the Bombay High Court and Delhi High Court confirming that this retroactive provision applies to applications that were already filed and remaining pending under adjudication. In practice, compliance workflows and ongoing proceedings must account for the fact that interim moratoriums for personal guarantors ceased to operate as of May 26, 2026 for pending applications.
takeaway: Review ongoing insolvency resolution processes involving personal guarantors to corporate debtors to ensure alignment with the cessation of the interim moratorium effective from May 26, 2026.
